name: Louisville Muhammad Ali International
subtitle: Stand assignment and push control for Concourses A and B and UPS Worldport Ramps 1-11
source: Concourse stands and headings, taxiways, aprons and buildings from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL): each stand 20 m back from the jet-bridge end of its lead-in line. Gate list from the Jeppesen 10-9 (23 OCT 26, user-supplied); A3A, which OSM lacks, sits between the A3 and A5 lead-ins as on the 10-9 inset. UPS Worldport stand numbers and ramps from ForeFlight (user screenshots), georeferenced to the X-Plane Scenery Gateway KSDF airport (startup locations, 2024): where a Gateway spot lies within 25 m of a ForeFlight stand, the stand takes the Gateway position and heading; the rest are placed from the screenshots (a few metres to ~15 m) with headings from their lead-in lines. Stand ids are <ramp>-<number> (3-07 is Ramp 3 stand 07). Generated frames: north up, 1.5 m/px, linear in lat/lon.
airlinesSource: Approximate: the passenger airlines split across both concourses (the airport does not publish gate assignments). UPS on the Worldport ramps, the finger ramps first.
notes: No ramp control frequencies are published; the stand telex is just the stand. Ground 121.7, Tower 124.2, Clearance 126.1.

UPS Worldport stands are <ramp>-<number>: Ramp 1 north of the A finger west, Ramp 2 north of the A finger east, Ramps 3/5/7 between the west fingers, Ramp 4 south of the A finger east, Ramp 6 the apron rows east, Ramp 9 south of the Worldport, Ramp 11 the west and middle apron south.
A3A shares its space with A3 and A5.
